feed.title: Ledger Monitor updates
feed.subtitle: New dashboards, data refreshes and features from Ledger Monitor.
feed.rights: Data: CC BY 4.0 compilation. Code: MIT.

entry.title: New dashboard: Wages & the Cost of Living
entry.summary: 7.9% of the world's workers, nearly 300 million people, live on less than $3 a day. The new dashboard sets minimum and average wages (ILOSTAT, OECD) against prices: in 55 of 131 countries a healthy diet for one person costs a quarter or more of the minimum wage. It also tracks pay after inflation, working poverty, labour's share of income and, for the UK, real earnings and the National Living Wage.

entry.title: New dashboard: Floods, Disasters & Insurance Gaps
entry.summary: 1.81 billion people live where a once-a-century flood would reach them. The new dashboard, a companion to Extreme Heat, shows who is exposed to flooding (World Bank study, Nature Communications), how often disasters force people from their homes (IDMC), what disasters killed and cost in 2025 (CRED), how much of the loss was insured (Munich Re, Swiss Re), and England's flood risk (Environment Agency).

entry.title: Housing: UBS bubble risk updated to 2026
entry.summary: The bubble-risk ratings now come from the UBS Global Real Estate Bubble Index 2026, which covers 23 cities, including Seoul and Lisbon for the first time. Zurich and Tokyo are the only cities at high risk; Miami, top of the index for the previous two editions, drops to elevated. Hong Kong, the least affordable market in the Demographia survey, rises from low to moderate. The links to the Demographia reports, which had moved, are fixed; their figures were checked against the reports and are unchanged.

entry.title: Food: what households spend on food, updated to 2025
entry.summary: Food's share of household spending now comes straight from the US Department of Agriculture's August 2026 edition, with 2025 figures for 103 countries (2023 before). Nigeria still spends the most, 56% of household budgets; Singapore (6.3%) now spends less than the United States (6.4%). ERS now uses Oxford Economics data, so some countries, such as Bangladesh and Venezuela, differ a lot from the previous edition.

entry.title: Two new dashboards, rebuild scripts for every dashboard, and data corrections
entry.summary: Fertiliser Prices & Supply (World Bank, FAOSTAT and Defra) and The Cost of Sending Money Home (World Bank Remittance Prices Worldwide and the UN SDG database) join the monitor. Every dashboard can now be rebuilt from its raw downloads. Rebuilding the Internet data fixed a duplicate cable and three misread cable lengths, so 26 countries, not 27, hang on a single cable; the Air dashboard now labels WHO's figure as urban areas and credits the Air Quality Life Index for pollution from human sources.

entry.title: Three new dashboards: Medicines, Household Energy and Vaccination
entry.summary: Medicine Shortages & Supply (FDA, EMA, UN Comtrade and NHS data), Household Energy Prices & Poverty (World Bank, Eurostat, Ofgem and DESNZ) and Vaccination & Health Workers (WHO/UNICEF coverage estimates, WHO workforce data and UKHSA) join the monitor, each with a script to rebuild its tables and figures on the country profiles.

entry.title: Country profiles, comparisons, search and embeddable charts
entry.summary: Every country now has a profile page that brings its figures from all the dashboards together, each cited and ranked against other countries. You can compare up to four countries side by side, search the hub for a country, dashboard or mineral, and embed any dashboard's headline chart on your own site.

entry.title: Four new dashboards: Food, Debt, Heat and Critical Minerals
entry.summary: Food Prices & Hunger, Debt vs Public Services, Extreme Heat and Critical Minerals join the monitor, each built from FAO, IMF, World Bank, Copernicus, USGS and IEA data, with scripts to rebuild their tables from fresh downloads.

entry.title: Eight open-data dashboards
entry.summary: Chokepoints, Electricity Mix & Grid Carbon, The Air We Breathe, Housing Affordability, Water Stress, The Scam Economy, Where the Internet Lives and Who Owns Orbit, with every number linked to its source and all data free to download.
